expected_theory_side_corrections.As_NLO_relation_assumed: A_s = V(phi)/(24 pi^2 eps_V(phi)) (Mbar=1 shape units) compared with the leading A_s ~ 1/(24 pi^2 * 3/(4N^2)); both terms (V and eps_V) receive O(1/N) fractional corrections, independently rederived from the same phi(N) inversion used for n_s above.
expected_theory_side_corrections.As_NLO_sign_note: POSITIVE: exact slow-roll predicts MORE A_s than the leading formula at fixed N, i.e. the wrong sign to explain the amplitude-vs-tilt tension (which needs A_s reduced, k<1, at the tilt-preferred N).
expected_theory_side_corrections.relation_assumed: n_s - 1 = -6 eps_V + 2 eta_V (standard slow-roll, e.g. Liddle & Lyth, 'Cosmological Inflation and Large-Scale Structure', CUP 2000; Starobinsky potential V=(3/4)M^2(1-e^{-sqrt(2/3)phi})^2, Starobinsky 1980), rederived independently by numeric quadrature of N(phi)=int V/V' dphi and root-finding phi(N), not by hand and not imported. The reported shift is n_s^exact(N) - (1-2/N), evaluated directly at each N of interest (not an asymptotic 1/N^2 fit).

reheating_Nrange.equation: ln k_* = -N_* + (1/3) ln(rho_reh/rho_end) + ln(T0/T_reh) + (1/3) ln(g_{s,0}/g_star) + ln H_*
reheating_Nrange.note_on_1e16_endpoint: 1e16 GeV exceeds the physical instantaneous-reheating ceiling T_reh_max=2.596e+15 GeV set by rho_end for this fixed potential normalisation (M^2/Mbar^2=c3^7); T_reh is capped at T_reh_max before use, so the N* value reported at the 1e16 GeV grid endpoint below equals the instantaneous-reheating value.
reheating_Nrange.source: Starobinsky 1980; Vilenkin 1985; Gorbunov & Panin 2010 (standard pivot-scale reheating-matching equation); potential normalisation M^2/Mbar^2=c3^7 fixed by the c3 axiom elsewhere in the theory.

amplitude_branch_N56.note: amplitude-preferred N is 1.011 e-folds above the instantaneous-reheating ceiling N_max=55.612 found here; it sits just outside, not inside, the reheating-allowed band.

tilt_branch_N80.note: tilt-preferred N exceeds the same ceiling by 25.03 e-folds -- far outside, independent of any amplitude tension.

survives_correction_budget.verdict: n_s channel: reaching p>0.05 needs an additive shift delta_n_s=0.00464 (1.55 x the ACT sigma); the independently rederived exact-slow-roll NLO-and-beyond shift at this N is only 0.00128, i.e. 3.63 x too small (same sign, wrong size). A_s channel: reaching p>0.05 needs a -24.5% multiplicative shift on A_s (equivalently a -3.94% shift in the fixed c3 -- not itself a slow-roll-correctable quantity since c3 is an axiom -- vs the exact central-value-matching figure of -9.61% from the prior round); the independently rederived exact-slow-roll NLO fractional correction on A_s at this N is +10.31%, i.e. it has the WRONG SIGN (predicts MORE A_s, the fit needs LESS) and is 2.4 x too small in magnitude even ignoring the sign. Reheating channel: the amplitude-preferred N=56.624 sits 1.011 e-folds above, and the tilt-preferred N=80.645 sits 25.03 e-folds above, the instantaneous-reheating ceiling N<=55.612 found for T_reh in [1e3,1e16] GeV at this fixed potential normalisation -- both lie outside the reheating-allowed range, the tilt branch by roughly 25 e-folds. CONCLUSION: none of the three correction channels actually on offer (NLO n_s, NLO A_s, reheating N) closes the joint-fit tension; the tilt-preferred branch (N=80.6) is additionally and independently excluded by the reheating e-fold budget regardless of the amplitude tension.

parameter_deficit.conclusion: A single Gaussian width sigma traces a one-dimensional curve in the (m2/m3, m1/m3) plane. Fitting 2 independent observed mass ratios (charged-lepton or up-quark) needs at least 2 independent real parameters; only 1 (sigma) is available in this profile family, so the parameter deficit counted here is 1 (need >=2, have 1). This holds independently on both the L=8 and L=10 flux-3 rebuilds.
parameter_deficit.parameters_available_description: one Gaussian-profile width sigma, shared by both L=8 and L=10 flux-3 rebuilds

up_quark.source: PDG 2024 (Particle Data Group); m_u, m_c in the MSbar scheme, m_t the pole mass -- used only for an order-of-magnitude hierarchy comparison, not a scheme-matched fit.

joint_fit.dof_naive_convention: 3 observables minus 1 parameter (naive count, not used as the headline number)
joint_fit.dof_primary_convention: 2 two-sided data points (n_s, ln(10^10 A_s)) minus 1 fitted parameter (N) = 1. The one-sided r<0.038 term contributes 0 to chi2 and 0 gradient whenever it is not violated (it is not a real constraint on N in that regime), so it is excluded from the dof count used for the headline p-value; it is still added to chi2_total (as 0 here) and reported on its own in the tensor-prediction section.
